about.title: Citrus Heights Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should not be something you carry alone. In Citrus Heights, defective goods turn up in ordinary places: a space heater in a home off Auburn Boulevard, a power tool bought along Sunrise Boulevard, a child's car seat riding down Greenback Lane. When one of those items has a flaw in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, California law generally lets you hold the companies behind it strictly liable. You usually do not have to prove anyone was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. Manufacturers, distributors, and the retailer who sold it can each share responsibility. Public records show 310 injury collisions in Citrus Heights during 2025, with 408 people hurt, and a share of crashes anywhere raise questions about airbags, tires, or brakes that did not perform as intended. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Citrus Heights Residents Use LawProactive

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: For many defective-product claims in California, the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving the manufacturer was negligent. The attorneys we connect you with know how to frame a claim around that standard.

items.title: Every link in the supply chain can be accountable
items.desc: The maker, the distributor, and the Citrus Heights or online retailer that sold the item may each be responsible. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Preserving the product matters
items.desc: The item itself is often the most important piece of evidence, so keeping it exactly as it is can shape the entire case. Your attorney can arrange safe storage and expert inspection.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Citrus Heights, not from the manufacturer. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: Yes. California law allows claims against retailers and distributors as well as manufacturers, so the shop on Greenback Lane or Antelope Road where you made the purchase may be part of the case. An attorney can help identify every company in the chain. Hold onto your receipt or any purchase record if you have one.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company did something wrong?
items.answer: Usually not in the way you might expect. Under strict liability, you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careful is often beside the point.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it, and do not repair it, throw it away, or return it to the store. Take photos of the item, the packaging, and any instructions or warnings that came with it. Your attorney will likely want it examined by an expert, and the original condition matters.
